content.text:
**Finding: compliant (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

The licence architecture in Section 13, read with Section 24.1, satisfies every preferred element:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Extends to affiliates | § 13.1 ("Customer, its Affiliates"); § 13.2 |
| Extends to contractors acting on our behalf | § 13.1 ("contractors acting on their behalf") |
| Paid-up licence perpetual | § 13.2 ("perpetual") |
| Paid-up licence irrevocable | § 13.2 ("irrevocable") |
| Subscription terminable only for uncured material breach | § 13.3 (no revocation/suspension "except during a material uncured payment or use breach ... after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure") |
| Transferable to successors | § 13.3 + § 24.1 (assignment to a successor in merger/reorganization/acquisition/asset sale without Vendor consent) |

Affiliate coverage is granted outright rather than gated on written notice, so the clause sits above the fallback.

One cross-reference noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged here: § 14.2 gives us only a "revocable, non-transferable licence" in Deliverables for the Order Form term, which pulls against §§ 13.2–13.3 (and is partly rescued for embedded Vendor Technology by § 14.3). That is a Deliverable ownership/licence issue and belongs to the IP rule — flagging it under this rule as well would double-count the same commercial term.
